title: Erdős Problem #136: The Erdős-Gyárfás Function f(n,4,5)
description: Minimum colors to edge-color Kₙ so every K₄ has ≥5 colors among its 6 edges. Answer: f(n) ~ (5/6)n. Erdős-Gyárfás bounds: (5/6)(n-1) < f(n) < n. Resolved by Bennett et al. (2022).

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős and Gyárfás introduced the function f(n,p,q), defined as the minimum number of colors needed to edge-color the complete graph Kₙ so that every Kₚ subgraph contains at least q distinct colors. For the specific case f(n,4,5), they proved the bounds (5/6)(n-1) < f(n) < n and computed f(9) = 8.

The problem remained open for 25 years until Bennett, Cushman, Dudek, and Pralat (2022) proved that f(n) ~ (5/6)n, confirming Erdős's intuition that the lower bound is asymptotically tight. Joos and Mubayi independently found a shorter proof using connections to hypergraph matching theory.

The constant 5/6 arises naturally from the structure of K₄: it has C(4,2) = 6 edges, and requiring at least 5 colors means at most one repeated color is allowed. The fraction 5/6 = 1 - 1/6 reflects this single 'defect' tolerance per K₄ subgraph.
overview.problemStatement: Let f(n) be the smallest number of colors needed to color edges of Kₙ such that every K₄ contains at least 5 different colors. Determine f(n).
overview.text: Minimum colors to edge-color Kₙ so every K₄ has ≥5 colors among its 6 edges. Answer: f(n) ~ (5/6)n. Erdős-Gyárfás bounds: (5/6)(n-1) < f(n) < n. Resolved by Bennett et al. (2022).
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines edge colorings, the K₄ constraint, and f(n) as the minimum via Nat.find. Erdős-Gyárfás bounds are axiomatized, along with the 2022 asymptotic resolution f(n)/n → 5/6. The summary theorem proves the conjunction of the asymptotic limit and both original bounds.
keyInsights: K₄ has C(4,2) = 6 edges, requiring ≥5 colors means at most 1 repeated color
The fraction 5/6 naturally arises as 1 - 1/6 (one 'defect' allowed)
Bennett et al. and Joos-Mubayi proved f(n) ~ (5/6)n — the lower bound is tight
The ε-δ formalization of f(n)/n → 5/6 makes the asymptotic result precise: for any ε > 0, eventually |f(n)/n - 5/6| < ε — bridging informal 'asymptotically' language to a machine-checkable statement

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #136 is SOLVED. The Erdős-Gyárfás function f(n,4,5) satisfies f(n) ~ (5/6)n, confirming Erdős's intuition that the lower bound is tight. The constant 5/6 reflects that K₄ has 6 edges and we require 5 colors.
conclusion.implications: This result settles a fundamental question in Ramsey-type graph coloring. The techniques developed connect graph coloring to hypergraph matchings.
openQuestions: What is the exact second-order term in f(n) = (5/6)n + o(n)?
What are the asymptotics for general f(n,p,q)?
Can the hypergraph matching technique extend to other Ramsey problems?
